sdkVersionAtPass._measured: installed versions, read from node_modules — not the package.json ranges

decisions.chose: leave every surface on the host's --civitai-* tokens
decisions.because: src/theme.ts already resolves every colour to a host token with zero hardcoded values, so light/dark correctness is the platform's. Moving to `skin` would transfer that debt to this app for no gain the store assets do not already provide — the #00AB89 plate is the brand's expression in the STORE, not in a block whose job is to render other people's images side by side. Notably the theme module already avoids the --civitai-color-gray-* ramp on purpose because it is theme-INVARIANT.

decisions.what: no in-app hero image, despite hero generation being pre-authorised
decisions.because: the app's primary object is a comparison grid inside a fixed-height iframe (minHeight 640). A hero band would push the grid down on every visit for an app people re-enter to check results. Same reasoning that kept sensei heroless. The store listing already carries generated cover art; a second hero inside the block is dead pixels on visit two.

decisions.what: vote state moved from a per-viewer KV mirror to the host's viewerVoted flag
decisions.because: the mirror was written only by the client that cast the vote, so it could not see another tab/session/device and nothing could reconcile a disagreement. Verified the host flag is DEPLOYED before relying on it (civitai#3474 is an ancestor of the running dp-prod build 5.1.68/bbbe837), rather than trusting the SDK type.

decisions.what: report() is escalation only — no owner-side hide was added
decisions.chose: offer Report, and say plainly that it does not remove the row
decisions.because: constraints §6: update/withdraw are author-scoped, so the app owner has no server-side power to hide another viewer's row, and report() explicitly does not hide it either. The alternative — a client-side soft-hide honoured by an owner-authored ledger — is real but is a much larger change and would need naming as suppression rather than deletion. Not warranted for a board this size today.

decisions.what: the board-scan page cap now discloses itself
decisions.chose: surface a notice rather than raise the cap or add a 'load more'
decisions.because: constraints §2 — there is no server-side sort, so any ranking is client-side over what was read. The cap (2000 rows) does not bind today (~22 live rows), so raising it would be tuning a constraint that is not binding; what was actually wrong was that crossing it was SILENT. An honest partial beats a confident wrong order.

decisions.chose: leave the app motionless, so prefers-reduced-motion is n/a rather than passed
decisions.because: the app ships zero transitions/animations today. Adding motion purely so the rubric's reduced-motion item could be marked 'pass' would be inventing work to grade. If motion is added later, the reduced-motion test becomes mandatory.

deferred.what: requester/author identity on a row — cards show no handle for the submitter
deferred.blockedBy: constraints §5 — the listed item carries authorUserId as a bare number and there is no user lookup; the only identity scope is user:read:self, which reads the VIEWER not the author.
deferred.closingCondition: A host message type that resolves a userId to a public handle ships in @civitai/blocks-react and appears in the installed .d.ts. Checked mechanically by grepping the installed types for such a method during the next pass's phase 0; until then this is platform work, not app work.

deferred.what: an owner-side hide for abusive rows, so the app author can suppress without waiting for a platform moderator
deferred.blockedBy: constraints §6 — update/withdraw reject FORBIDDEN for anyone but the row's author, and report() does not hide.
deferred.closingCondition: Either the host gains an owner-scoped moderation capability (visible in the installed UseSharedStorage .d.ts), OR a moderation incident on this board makes the client-side soft-hide ledger worth its complexity. The second is a judgement over named evidence: the app owner reads the reported-row queue and decides.
